On 2026-09-23, released 11.7.0-2 with patch 0005, which makes RecipeOptions::inherit tokenize merged *_args without keeping quotes. At 3d5991033 the merge wrapped quoted values in their quote characters and then quoted them again, so llama-server received a literal '{"preserve_thinking":true}' for the qwen35 and qwen35moe --chat-template-kwargs architecture default and exited. The distro defaults always set --no-mmap, so every qwen35 and qwen35moe model failed to load. The regression is fork-only: fork commit e3d08ffa6 added quote_custom_arg_value to map_to_args_string, which stacks on upstream's keep_quotes=true merge (lemonade-sdk/lemonade#1920), while upstream v11.6.0, v11.7.0, and v11.9.0 produce the correct argv. The fork fix is nisavid/lemonade#168; drop patch 0005 at the Lemonade repin to a fork commit that contains #168, which is the upstream-synced fork main that the issue 141 (M6) repackage adopts. Upstream #3265 (7b5657d80, first released in v11.8.0) is context only: it moves the merge to recipe_arg_resolver.h, which still keeps quotes, so it does not fix the fork. Issues 139 and 140 track the regression.

On 2026-09-25, repinned the source to the merge commit of the fork's upstream v11.9.0 sync (issue 141, nisavid/lemonade#175) and set the package version to 11.9.0. The sync contains upstream v11.9.0 (bb39eaf) and the fork fix for nisavid/lemonade#168 (2cb1a91, PR 169), so patch 0005 is dropped. Patches 0001-0004 apply unchanged to the new base with line offsets only and no fuzz; the upstream changes in the patched files do not touch the patched hunks.

On 2026-09-25, followed the 11.9 service layout (issue 141): the 30-env-files.conf drop-in keeps /etc/lemonade/conf.d/*.conf loading ahead of upstream's /etc/default/lemond and loads the packaged llama.cpp env file (moved out of conf.d) last; both secrets files are backup files; no install script writes owner config; and the distro defaults gained max_loaded_models -1 and an explicit auto_update_models false. The owner's deploy steps (a sparse config.json with the host binding, and verifying the JSON migration into /var/lib/lemonade) belong to the issue 141 redeploy.

policy.pkgdesc: Local AI server runtime rebuilt for Strix Halo gfx1151
scaffold_notes: Server/runtime package; llama.cpp backends are optdepends, not hard deps.

Builds the delivered v11.9.0 per-model executable-binding backport, nisavid/lemonade commit 0101b6938c0e77ffaf73687165518a2f8fd672b0 (nisavid/lemonade#208), whose CMake project version remains 11.9.0. The shared lemonade source pin keeps server and app coupled. The independent fork-main and upstream-release observations remain freshness inputs, not source selections.
Configures with BUILD_TESTING=OFF; upstream includes CTest, and the distro build does not need its C++ test binaries.
Uses upstream's lemond.service unit name; do not ship the pre-10.3 lemonade-server.service name in this package.

Uses upstream's lemond.service as installed. Since 11.9 it sets StateDirectory=lemonade (the config dir: config.json, user_models.json, recipe_options.json, jobs.json, mcp_servers.json), CacheDirectory=lemonade with mode 0755 (bin/ and aliases.json), a bare ExecStart=/usr/bin/lemond, and EnvironmentFile=-/etc/default/lemond as its only EnvironmentFile= line, and upstream installs no lemond.service.d drop-in. package() fails the build if the unit loses that layout or upstream installs any file under lemond.service.d/ (checked before the package installs its own drop-ins), because a cache-dir argument or a LEMONADE_CACHE_DIR, HOME, or XDG_* override would make the config dir follow the cache dir, and because 30-env-files.conf resets the EnvironmentFile= list and would silently drop any other upstream entry, including one in an upstream drop-in that sorts before it. On first start lemond moves the five JSON files from the legacy /var/lib/lemonade/.cache/lemonade into /var/lib/lemonade without overwriting, and the rest of that tree into /var/cache/lemonade.

Installs /usr/lib/systemd/system/lemond.service.d/30-env-files.conf, which owns the service's whole EnvironmentFile= order. It first resets the list with an empty EnvironmentFile=, because systemd keeps a repeated path at its first position, so listing /etc/default/lemond again without the reset would not move it after conf.d. It then lists -/etc/lemonade/conf.d/*.conf, -/etc/default/lemond, and the required /usr/lib/lemonade/llamacpp-gfx1151.env. systemd reads them in that order and a later file overrides an earlier one, so /etc/default/lemond overrides conf.d, a key set only in conf.d still applies, and the package env file overrides any stale LEMONADE_LLAMACPP_* key in the owner files.

Installs /usr/lib/lemonade/llamacpp-gfx1151.env so the packaged ROCm and Vulkan llama.cpp wrapper binaries are exposed to the service as system-managed backends. lemond reads LEMONADE_LLAMACPP_*_BIN from the environment ahead of config.json on every backend lookup, so the refreshed system-managed backend patch no longer carries the older config-load environment overlay or the CLI backend-table change.

Exports the packaged llama.cpp revision and ggml release URL in the same env file so the GUI shows the packaged backend metadata instead of upstream downloader defaults. Through 11.7 these lived in /etc/lemonade/conf.d/10-llamacpp-gfx1151.conf, with the same values; the metadata patch reads them only from the environment. To override a LEMONADE_LLAMACPP_* key, add an owner drop-in under /etc/systemd/system/lemond.service.d/ that sorts after 30-env-files.conf, such as 40-llamacpp-override.conf, with its own EnvironmentFile= line, which systemd reads after the package env file. An Environment= line there does not override the key, because every EnvironmentFile= value overrides Environment=.
The system-managed backend patch probes llama-server --version through Lemonade's argv-based ProcessManager capture path, not a shell.

Marks upstream's /etc/default/lemond (mode 0640, the service's HF_TOKEN, LEMONADE_API_KEY, and LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY file) and /etc/lemonade/conf.d/zz-secrets.conf (mode 0660) as backup files so an upgrade keeps local edits. Upstream 11.9 no longer installs zz-secrets.conf, so the package ships 11.7's placeholder byte for byte: an owner-edited copy stays in place without a .pacnew and keeps loading through the conf.d glob. If the package dropped it, pacman would rename an edited copy to zz-secrets.conf.pacsave, which the glob does not match. The llama.cpp env file stays package-owned so each release refreshes the backend metadata.

No install script writes owner config: nothing is merged into /etc/default/lemond. Moving settings from conf.d into /etc/default/lemond is optional, because conf.d keeps loading. Since 11.9, LEMONADE_* settings in either file only seed a config.json that does not exist yet, so server settings such as the host binding belong in config.json.

Installs a sparse /usr/share/lemonade/defaults.json with only no_fetch_executables=true and the packaged llama.cpp backend, prefer_system, rocm_bin, and vulkan_bin settings. lemond merges it over built-in descriptor/resource defaults and under config.json; an optional LEMONADE_DEFAULTS_PATH is another defaults layer. Owner configuration retains precedence, and matching values are pruned on config writes. The package does not set offline, auto_update_models, max_loaded_models, or llama.cpp loading arguments. At the selected fork's source defaults, auto_update_models remains false and max_loaded_models is 1; these are inherited source values, not new household settings. Host binding, residency policy, and actual backend compatibility retain their installation/qualification checks.

Leaves model-download endpoints unmodified and ships no 20-no-remote-model-fetch.conf. Validation must prove the selected packaged engine and intended model supplied the result; an unintended downloaded engine or fallback cannot satisfy a gate. No install script writes household configuration.

Uses Arch's official lemonade pkgbase as the packaging comparison: 11.9.0-2 at 62c9d8dcdd819f3ecf2fd2eb0d05ab124dd888fa (https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/lemonade/-/blob/62c9d8dcdd819f3ecf2fd2eb0d05ab124dd888fa/PKGBUILD). The newer 2026.42.1-1 comparison at 95f6e76558a7c0f21c2fccd8c05d76b224c0a426 does not select a new fork source. Neither recipe adds a defaults overlay or model-endpoint block; its two patches concern sysusers and web-app icons. This comparison supplies no runtime compatibility result.
Removes /usr/share/metainfo because the web-app MetaInfo names lemonade-web-app.desktop as its launchable, and this package removes that desktop entry.

recipe.notes:
Lemonade is a unified inference server wrapping llama.cpp (GPU/CPU),
FLM (NPU), and ONNX backends behind an OpenAI-compatible API.

The project split in v10: the git repo (v10.0.0) is a C++ server,
while the Python SDK is published separately as lemonade-sdk on PyPI
(v9.1.4). The SDK handles llama-server process management, model
downloads, .env loading, and hardware detection.

Version pin fixes: lemonade-sdk pins huggingface-hub==0.33.0,
onnx==1.18.0, transformers<=4.53.2 which conflict with vLLM.
Reinstalling at compatible versions resolves conflicts.
